articles.title: 2026 RLBC Season Review
articles.summary: Darren Mabbott looks back on the 2026 season: the Wolves’ three-peat, the Dragons’ 9s win, the Trent ‘Bones’ Bourke Memorial Cup and BC players on the Canada Wolverines tour.
articles.image_alt: 2026 RLBC season results, first grade men
articles.body:
By Darren Mabbott

The 2026 RLBC season started with 4 teams in the main competition, with the Valley Warriors taking the season out to re-group and prepare for the 2027 season. The Valley Vipers, Vancouver Dragons, and Point Grey Thunder looked to stop the Whistler Wolves from achieving the three-peat by winning their third championship. There was also a lot to play for with regards to International Honours, the Canada Wolverines looking forward to a 3-match tour to Europe to take on Norway, Scotland, and the Netherlands, as well as a Home International against Jamaica. There were places up for grabs in the Canada Rugby League East v West match in Brampton, Ontario. There were also places up for grabs for the Under 19s team taking part in their first U19 European tournament where they would face Norway U19, Greece U19 and Ireland U19 in France, and there were places for the Canada Ravens tour to Wales and Scotland.

The season started with the RLBC nines tournament, which was played at the famous Brockton Oval in Vancouver, where the 4 main domestic teams took place in a league table format, with the top 2 teams, the Vancouver Dragons and the Valley Vipers, battling hard in the final, and the Dragons came out the victors winning 20-10, winning the first piece of silverware up for grabs. Also at the nines tournament, the Vancouver Dragons and Whistler Wolves 2nd teams took to the field in a hard-fought match which shows the future of the RLBC is heading in the right direction.

On May 30th, battle commenced with a repeat of the previous year’s final between the Vipers and the Wolves, and the Wolves started their championship defence with a 34-20 victory, and the Thunder defeated the Dragons 34-30. The battle continued in week 2 when the Wolves beat the Dragons 58-6 to further strengthen their grip on the Minor Premiership, and in the second match the Thunder picked up their second win of the season beating the Vipers 38-34. At the end of week 3, the halfway point of the season, the Wolves again added to the win column with a victory against the Thunder, and the Dragons won the battle of the winless teams by beating the Vipers 46-30. In week 4, the re-matches began with a Thunder win over the Dragons 30-28, and the Wolves did the double over the Vipers 42-18, adding yet another victory to the column. Week 5 started with the Wolves defeating the Thunder 66-4 and were 1 game away from an undefeated regular season while winning the Minor Premiership, and the winless Vipers got their first win of the season defeating the Dragons 40-36. In the final week of the season all 4 teams were in with a shout of the 3 playoff places, the Wolves already securing 1st place and the bye week only just defeated the Dragons 24-22, and the Vipers had to make sure of victory to finish in 3rd place, and they achieved that goal by beating the Thunder 46-10, and with that the regular season ended, now the hard work began trying to stop the Wolves from their three-peat. The RLBC Qualifying final was a repeat of the final game of the season and was another win for the Vipers 30-22 over the Thunder, booking the place in the final and being the only team who could stop the Wolves charge to a third RLBC Championship. July 25th, 2026, was the date, Burnaby Lake Rugby Club was the venue, and the battle for the Championship would be decided by the valiant warriors of the Valley Vipers and the Whistler Wolves. In a close fought match, the Wolves did the three-peat by defeating the Vipers 28-14, with this victory the Wolves joined RLBC 3 in a row winners Surrey Beavers (2012-2014) and the Point Grey Thunder (2021-2023). The Coastal Cougars also won 3 Championships but not in succession (2015, 2016 and 2019).

At the start of the season, the RLBC decided to honour former player Trent ‘Bones’ Bourke. Trent played for the Surrey Beavers and Abbotsford Griffins in the RLBC, Wentworth Magpies and Jamberoo Superoos in Australia, and he also represented the British Columbia Bulldogs and Canada Wolverines. Trent Bourke passed away in 2016. He was very dedicated to Rugby League in Canada and we would always have conversations about Rugby League, be it about the Keighley Cougars, British Columbia Rugby League or just general conversation about rugby league. Trent was a great friend, and the Trent ‘Bones’ Bourke Memorial Cup is a great tribute. The Memorial Cup first match was played June 6th when the Wolves beat the Dragons 58-6, and then defended the trophy July 4th, beating the Thunder 66-4. The Memorial Cup can only be defended at home, and the way to win the Cup is to beat the holders away from home.

With the Canada Wolverines European tour taking place from July 2nd to July 11th, there were 10 British Columbia players who represented the Wolverines, with Whistler Wolves player Blake Mahovic captaining the Wolverines, while Valley Vipers player Jalen Harrison was top points scorer with 22 points on the tour. To show the strength in depth of the RLBC, the U19 Wolverines had 17 players involved in the European Championships, with Valley Vipers player Oliver Lenahan scoring a massive 40 points in the tournament, which shows he is a player for the future.

The representative honours were still available to the players of British Columbia with the yearly East v West match, which the West lost 16-52 in Brampton, Ontario.

To further develop the future of rugby league in British Columbia, they are introducing an Under 19s winter league which will have 4 teams playing 6 matches each, and for the players to show they are the future of British Columbia and Canada Rugby League.

About the author: This report was written by Darren Mabbott and contributed to Rugby League BC.

articles.title: Women’s provincial championships at Burnaby Lake
articles.summary: Darren Mabbott reports on the 4th annual Canada Rugby League Women’s provincial championships, held May 15 to 17 at Burnaby Lake, with the Alberta Broncos defending their title.
articles.image_alt: BC Storm women's squad posing together in RLBC blue and gold kit
articles.body:
By Darren Mabbott

The 4th annual Canada Rugby League Women’s provincial championships took place over the weekend of May 15th – 17th in beautiful Burnaby Lake, British Columbia. Defending Champions the Alberta Broncos, 2-time champions the Ontario Ospreys and the host British Columbia Storm, all ever present in the competition in the last 3 years, were ready to lock horns and do battle on the field of play to become the 2026 Women’s provincial champions.

The first match took place on Friday May 15th between the Alberta Broncos and the British Columbia Storm. Broncos head coach Dennis Wickliffe had the defending champions primed and ready to go, while Storm head coach Francis Denny had his team ready to register their first win since the opening match of the 2023 Championships. Both teams looked very good, but the defending champions came away with the win 42-8. Current Canada Ravens players Maddy Aberg, Dani Franada and Brittany Jones, as well as newcomer Agnes Tse, put in strong performances for the Broncos, while for the Storm Captain Gabrielle Hindley, Alayna Scramstad and newcomer Peyton McNeil put in good performances for the defeated hosts.

On Saturday May 16th, the Alberta Broncos, who were 1 win away from defending their title, took on 2-time champions the Ontario Ospreys. A close game was expected, and the players did not disappoint. The defending champion Alberta Broncos, with strong performances by Rebecca Kochuk, Captain Sarah Maguire and newcomer Larae Benoit, kept hold of their crown with a 24-10 win over Ontario, who had Canada Ravens players Tamisha Toussaint, Natasha Naismith and newcomer Tatiana Joseph putting in strong performances for the Ospreys.

The last game of the competition took place on Sunday May 17th, and was between the Storm and the Ospreys, who were both looking for their first win of the 2026 competition, and it was the Storm who achieved the victory with a 22-12 win over Ontario. Both teams showed signs of brilliant play and hard hitting tackles. British Columbia had Ravens player Ada Okonkwo lead from the front, with Dani Downey and Angelina Alexander backing up with their support play. Ontario had Captain Sara Canini, Beth Hofstetter and Lea Milsoovic organising the Ospreys on the field of play. Canada Ravens and Ontario Ospreys head coach Matt Barron said that the National Championships in Vancouver were a massive success and reinforced the growth we are seeing in women’s rugby league in Canada. The championship provides a competitive stage for players to be selected for the Canada Ravens program and ready them for representing Canada.

The Ontario Ospreys, British Columbia Storm and the Alberta Broncos are always looking for teams from all around the world to play in Toronto, Ottawa, Edmonton, Calgary and Vancouver, some of Canada’s biggest and most beautiful cities. Corrimal Cougars and the Queensland Maori are two teams who have come to Canada to tour and had a great time. If your club is interested in playing any of these teams, get in touch with RLBC.

About the author: This report was written by Darren Mabbott and contributed to Rugby League BC.

articles.title: Wellington Wedgetails are coming to Vancouver
articles.summary: From Wiradjuri Country to Coast Salish Territory: the Wedgetails meet the BC Bulldogs at Brockton Oval on Sunday, March 14, 2027.
articles.body:
From Wiradjuri Country to Coast Salish Territory. Two communities, one game. An ocean apart, connected through culture, community and rugby league.

Rugby League British Columbia is proud to welcome the Wellington Wedgetails from New South Wales, Australia, as they prepare to take on our very own BC Bulldogs in a special international rugby league clash on Sunday, March 14, 2027.

Match details

  • Match: Wellington Wedgetails vs BC Bulldogs
  • Date: Sunday, March 14, 2027
  • Venue: Brockton Oval, Stanley Park, Vancouver, BC
  • Kick-off: 4:00 PM

From Wiradjuri Country to the Coast Salish Territories

The Wellington Wedgetails come from the heart of Wiradjuri Country in central New South Wales, Australia.

Their hometown of Wellington sits within a region traditionally known as Binjang, meaning “the beautiful valley”, a place with thousands of years of Aboriginal history, culture and connection to Country.

For the Wedgetails, rugby league is more than a sport. It is an opportunity to celebrate their heritage, strengthen community ties and create opportunities for their players and future generations.

In March 2027, their journey will bring them across the Pacific Ocean to Vancouver, British Columbia, where they will be welcomed on the traditional, ancestral and unceded territories of the Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh Nations.

These Coast Salish Nations have cared for these lands and waters since time immemorial, maintaining rich cultural traditions, languages and connections to their ancestral territories.

The match will take place at Brockton Oval in Stanley Park, near Brockton Point, a place known by the Indigenous names spapəy̓əq / Pápiy̓eḵ and one of deep historical and cultural significance.

It is a fitting setting for two teams to come together in the spirit of respect, friendship and community.

More than just a game

Following their appearance at the Koori Knockout, one of Australia’s most significant Aboriginal rugby league gatherings, the Wedgetails are taking their next journey overseas.

Their international connections are already growing. In 2024, the Wedgetails travelled to New Zealand to face Wellington Māori in a memorable rugby league encounter that celebrated Indigenous identity, cultural exchange and the friendships that sport can create.

Their upcoming visit to Vancouver continues that journey.

The Wedgetails have expressed their hopes of connecting with local Indigenous communities, sharing stories and traditions, and building friendships that reach far beyond the football field.

For Rugby League BC, this closely reflects our own commitment to bringing people together through sport and creating opportunities for young people and their communities.

The BC Bulldogs are ready to welcome the Wedgetails

Representing British Columbia, the BC Bulldogs will proudly take the field against the visiting Wedgetails.

As Rugby League BC’s provincial representative team, the Bulldogs bring together players from across our rugby league community to represent British Columbia against visiting teams and other provincial sides.

While both teams will be determined to claim victory, the occasion represents something greater than the final score.

It is an opportunity to bring together people from different backgrounds, celebrate the cultural heritage of our visitors and recognize the Indigenous communities whose traditional territories will host this special occasion.

On the field, expect a passionate contest between two proud rugby league teams.

Off the field, we hope to create an occasion that celebrates culture, encourages connection and leaves both teams with memories and friendships to carry home.

Building connections across the Pacific

From Binjang in Wiradjuri Country to the Coast Salish territories of Vancouver, this journey reminds us of the power sport has to connect people across borders and oceans.

Rugby league has always been about more than the eighty minutes played on the field. It is about belonging, teamwork, respect and the communities that stand behind their players.

We hope this visit will help build lasting relationships between the Wellington Wedgetails, Rugby League BC and communities here in British Columbia.

Join us for a special day of rugby league

We invite the rugby league community, local Indigenous communities, families, supporters and the wider Vancouver public to join us in welcoming the Wellington Wedgetails to Canada.

Come along, support the BC Bulldogs and be part of an international occasion celebrating rugby league, culture, friendship and community.

Sunday, March 14, 2027 | Brockton Oval, Stanley Park | 4:00 PM

Two teams. Two countries. One shared love of rugby league. We look forward to welcoming the Wedgetails to Vancouver!

Wellington Wedgetails on Facebook

articles.title: Leigh Leopards linked to Vancouver rugby league visit
articles.summary: England’s Wigan & Leigh College is exploring a Vancouver stop on its February 2027 North American tour. The fixture is still subject to confirmation.
articles.body:
Excitement is building around a potential international rugby league visit to Vancouver in February 2027, with England’s Wigan & Leigh College exploring a stop in British Columbia as part of its North American tour.

The college, which has an established rugby league development partnership with Super League club Leigh Leopards, has received approval for its North American tour, with Vancouver among the destinations being considered.

The proposed visit could see the touring squad take on a BC representative side or one of our local clubs, offering British Columbia’s players an exciting opportunity to test themselves against international opposition on home soil.

With Leigh Leopards also confirmed to compete in Las Vegas in February 2027, it’s shaping up to be an exciting time for rugby league across North America.

Beyond the action on the field, a visit like this would strengthen international connections, showcase the growing talent in British Columbia and inspire the next generation of rugby league players.

Potential international rugby league fixture

  • Location: Vancouver, British Columbia
  • Proposed date: February 21, 2027
  • Visiting team: Wigan & Leigh College Rugby League
  • Local opposition, venue and kick-off: To be confirmed

While the Vancouver stopover and potential fixture remain subject to confirmation, the prospect of welcoming international rugby league talent to our province is certainly something to get excited about.

Stay tuned to Rugby League BC for further updates as plans develop!

Leigh Leopards website

articles.title: Dragons heading to Vegas
articles.summary: Vancouver Dragons will compete in the NRL Rugby League Vegas 9s on February 25 and 26, 2027, and are looking for sponsors and players.
articles.image_alt: A red dragon wrapped around the Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign
articles.body:
Vancouver Dragons will compete in the NRL Rugby League Vegas 9’s Tournament on February 25–26, 2027, taking a 9’s squad south of the border to represent British Columbia on the international stage.

The Dragons are currently seeking sponsors to support their Vegas campaign and are also welcoming expressions of interest from players interested in joining the squad.

Interested in getting involved?

For sponsorship or player enquiries, contact the Vancouver Dragons at secretary@vancouverdragons.ca or visit VancouverDragons.ca.

articles.title: Welcome to our 2027 board members
articles.summary: Following the AGM, RLBC announces its new and returning board members for the upcoming season.
articles.body:
Following a successful AGM with excellent representation from across the league, we are pleased to announce our new and returning board members for the upcoming season:

  • Josh Knight – President (continuing)
  • Richard Marshall – VP Rugby Development (continuing)
  • Vacant – VP Communication
  • Adam Timler – VP Finance (new)
  • Vacant – VP Sponsorship

We look forward to seeing all that our new and returning board members will accomplish this season.

If you would like to get in touch with a specific board member, please visit our board page. To contact the entire board, email board@rugbyleaguebc.ca.

articles.title: New to BC and looking for work?
articles.summary: Our community contacts at A&B Tool Rentals and Madden Solutions may be able to connect newcomers and overseas players with employment opportunities.
articles.body:
Moving to British Columbia and looking for work? Rugby League BC understands that finding employment can be one of the biggest challenges for players and newcomers arriving in the province.

We have relationships with local businesses that may be able to assist members of our rugby league community with employment opportunities.

A&B Tool Rentals

Employment opportunities may include:

  • General labour
  • Construction and trade opportunities
  • Short-term or seasonal work
  • Permanent employment

If you’re looking for work or would like to discuss available opportunities, contact A&B Tool Rentals through their website: abtoolrentals.com.

Madden Solutions

Madden Solutions may also have employment opportunities available for members of the Rugby League BC community, including moving, general labour and related work.

If you’re interested in employment opportunities, contact Madden Solutions directly through their website: www.maddensolutions.com.

Please note: Businesses listed on this page are independent businesses. Employment opportunities are subject to availability, experience and eligibility to work in Canada. Rugby League BC does not guarantee employment or act as an employment agency.
